scope: Real local Go tests and source edits in a controlled repeated PR/CI fixture. No remote GitHub PR, CI run, comment or branch was created.

methods.logs: Agent reads failed-test text and source files; it edits code and runs tests. Independent native verification follows. Reads/edits/tests may be batched.
methods.prepared: A producer gives structured failure deltas and full relevant current code in the prompt. The agent edits and tests; it may inspect files. Independent native verification follows.
methods.worker: The model returns replacement source as strict JSON, with no tools or edits. The native caller checks the preimage and path scope, applies/formats the content, then executes normal and independent tests.

commands: /bin/bash -lc 'pwd; rg --files -g AGENTS.md -g normalize.go -g go.mod; cat normalize.go'
/bin/bash -lc 'pwd && rg --files -g AGENTS.md -g normalize.go -g go.mod && cat normalize.go'
/bin/bash -lc "pwd && rg --files -g AGENTS.md -g branch.go -g '*test.go' -g go.mod -g '.ci/failure.log' -g '"'!vendor'"' && cat .ci/failure.log branch.go branch_test.go"
/bin/bash -lc 'pwd; rg --files -g AGENTS.md -g branch.go -g go.mod; cat branch.go'

event_gate.interpretation: This validates native handling of repeated/passed events. All arms use the same gate, so the six skipped events are not credited as a relative model-call reduction for any arm.

protocol.scope: Two local Go code repairs per simulated PR; eight CI observations per workflow. No remote GitHub writes.
protocol.common_gate: Both arms use the same native complete-report and verified-acknowledgement gate.

worker_protocol.mode: Model returns replacement JSON without tools; caller applies and tests.

findings.prepared_only: Passing a ready report and source code to a normal coding agent reduced mean total tokens only 2.27%. Some runs reread supplied files or performed more tool steps. Ranges overlap, and one logs workflow used an additional interaction.
findings.caller_managed_execution: The no-tool worker reduced total tokens 68.58% versus the logs agent and 67.85% versus the prepared agent for the two-repair fixture. Source application and testing were completed by the caller, not skipped.
findings.cache_tradeoff: The worker reported zero cached input in all six calls. Its mean uncached input was 30,018 per workflow, versus 9,658 for logs and 9,016 for prepared. Reduced total processing tokens do not establish lower billable input or monetary cost.
findings.interpretation: The observed processing-token benefit comes from removing model/tool round trips and finishing deterministic steps in native code. Merely formatting information as JSON did not yield the same benefit.
findings.packaging: A CLI, a skill script or an application can host this caller-managed protocol. Packaging alone is not the measured advantage.

limitations: Three workflows per arm, two small deterministic bug fixes each. These local controlled fixtures are not representative full-size GitHub PRs.
Stage two introduces new tests after stage one. Each repair uses a fresh model session; persistent model conversation effects are not measured.
The worker was added after initial methods revealed continued tool interactions, so its calls are not fully interleaved with the earlier methods.

Native preparation, report parsing, test execution, independent verification and benchmark setup tokens are excluded; those deterministic steps do not call the model. Parent-agent implementation and analysis costs are excluded.
Input-plus-output includes cached input. Cache behavior differs substantially between modes and per-request billing attribution is unavailable. No monetary savings are claimed.
Source and test text are bundled in the prepared/worker prompt. Providing equivalent context and caller-managed execution through another interface may produce similar savings.
The initial prepared packet repeats some failure data in both the full failure list and delta. The worker packet is smaller and uses a different output schema; both are part of the protocol change.
Model invocation counts are identical across arms; reductions are in input processed during tool interactions, not fewer repair tasks. Command item counts do not measure model HTTP request counts.
Source replacement is limited to a bounded, explicitly allowed file and matching preimage. Large changes, retries after failed proposals, conflicts and multi-file repairs remain unmeasured.

The native state protocol was tested for incomplete reports, modified revisions/new runs, evidence tampering, failed verification, panic evidence, source scope and preimage mismatch. It is a single-consumer prototype; concurrent state writers are unmeasured.
No model trials were discarded or retried; all nine workflows and eighteen proposals/repairs are reported.
CI config and producer were verified locally; Linux/macOS/Windows Actions jobs and artifact upload have not run remotely.

The current helper adds UTF-8 handling, panic evidence preservation and revision validation after the model experiment. The experiment protocol records the earlier source hashes; these changes do not alter the known fixture cases.
